audit.summary: Change class: large/sensitive (a database writer, state tables, destructive deletes, a CLI). 0 CRITICAL / 0 HIGH / 0 MEDIUM / 0 LOW. Dimensions covered: correctness, security, maintainability and test-adequacy. Verdict GO. Round-1 findings, each resolved in the code and pinned by a test: CR-PBI019-01 (HIGH). read_config and config_object turn a non-object or too-deeply-nested config into ValueError, so startup exits 2 ('not started'); a --once run gives no traceback; and in loop mode a config that cannot be re-read is a timestamped skipped pass and the loop goes on. The probe showed the same for a missing file, broken JSON and a bad local block, and sessions:[] reached run_pass's timestamped Refusal. Once a good config was saved, the next pass committed. The only config reload not caught is inside _one's catch-all, so loop mode cannot end on a config. CR-PBI019-02 (MEDIUM). _session_ok and _agent_ok now require the exact top-level key sets, the cursor field types and the result shape, so a bad row is a fresh entry. The reset is bounded: the rewritten row validates, and the test asserts the next pass opens nothing. Records are not lost: the session is fully re-derived and equals the exporter; the other session is not opened; the pass commits. CR-PBI019-03 (LOW). The connect is inside open_db's try with conn=None first, so a folder at the path is db.Refused and exit 2, and the lock case still goes to the lock path. CR-PBI019-04 (LOW). TakingTurns alternates a real --once subprocess with an in-process cached collector over 5 turns, asserting the seek to the other's cursor, counts equal to the turn, and exporter equivalence. The builder reports a mutation check that drops data_version, which is plausible since that assertion would fail. A lock-meets-pass test checks the timestamped spec 3.5 message. CR-PBI019-05 (LOW). _Pass.session went from 84 to 20 lines, and the largest helper is about 23. The try boundaries are as spec 4.3 and 4.4 prescribe: read_new through encode (in _stage, all encodes before anything is queued) sits inside the session's try; only _agent sits inside the agent's try; agent bookkeeping sits outside it; judge sits outside. FailedFeed, FailureAfterFeed and AC-64/AC-CL5 equivalence still pass, so the refactor is behaviour-preserving as far as the suites pin it. No regression found in AC-63 incremental reads, AC-64 equivalence, copy-then-swap, the guards or the opening sequence. The loop-mode choice (skip the pass rather than keep the last good config) conforms to spec 5; see follow_ups. Criteria: 24 of 25 met; the close-out criterion waits on a commit, and this gate is GO. Flag-only: nothing in the worktree was changed, staged, committed, run as a service or deployed.

follow_ups: Loop-mode call (the builder's question on CR-PBI019-01): skipping a pass on a config that cannot be re-read conforms to spec 5. It is a refused pass, reported with a timestamp, and the loop goes on, which matches --once, where a config error is an exit-2 refusal. Neither behaviour risks double-counting or losing records: a skipped pass writes nothing and moves no cursor, so the next good pass reads every appended byte once (asserted in ConfigFile and reproduced by the probe). Skipping is the safer choice, because it never runs on settings the owner has replaced, such as the exclude list. Its cost is a stall while the file stays bad: lastRefresh stops advancing and the reason is only on stderr. So the PBI-007 handoff to capture stderr is load-bearing, and the PBI-005 page should show the lastRefresh age. A stall left for weeks could outlast Claude Code's own transcript clean-up. Wording only: for a blank local.databasePath the message says the config 'could not be re-read' though it was read.

For the builder, optional hardening, beyond the spec 4.3 contract (key sets only): a stored row whose layout is valid but whose inner derive values have the wrong type still fails the whole pass on every pass. The probe showed this for state.cwd=123 with exclude set (AttributeError in derive.excluded, called from _Pass.excluded outside the session's try), result.doc.last=5 (derive.epoch in judge) and a result row without start (the sort in assemble). derive never writes these values (cwd is a string or None, last passes stamp(), rows always carry start), so only a hand edit or a future bug reaches them, which is why this is not raised as a finding. If wanted: turn any exception while interpreting one stored entry into a reset of that session.

Carried from round 1, optional and still open: in promote(), read PRAGMA data_version before COMMIT; the NaN line in Codec.test_generic_values_round_trip tests an empty list; the catalogue branch in guard() is unreachable through reasons().

For the spec owner, optional: spec 4.3 could say that a reset discards the stored result too. So an agent whose file fails during the reset pass has no row to carry, and its run is deleted as reason other (under the mass-delete guard) until it reads again.
